items.title: Dueling proofs from OpenAI and Anthropic astound scientists
items.excerpt: OpenAI and Anthropic released AI-generated results that claim to resolve major problems in math, physics and computer science, but like other recent AI 'slop drops' the releases are already controversial among researchers.
items.rationale: New concrete event: on the same day, OpenAI and Anthropic each released new AI-generated proofs. This is the one card for the proofs cluster and covers both labs plus researchers' pushback.

items.title: SPINE: A machine-learning program is on the trail of ghost particles
items.excerpt: SLAC's SPINE runs staged machine-learning models that find features in liquid-argon detector images, identify individual particles and rebuild whole neutrino interactions. It underpins ICARUS's first search for sterile-neutrino oscillation (arXiv 2603.22557).
items.rationale: Fresh particle-physics result in which ML reconstruction is central: SPINE drives ICARUS's first sterile-neutrino search.

items.title: Solving a 31-year-old grand challenge in mathematics: the KLS conjecture
items.excerpt: A Microsoft Research scientist and a collaborator proved the 1995 Kannan-Lovasz-Simonovits conjecture in high-dimensional convex geometry. They worked with AI agents in a structured, human-directed process that explored more than 100 candidate approaches before finding a recursive criterion.
items.rationale: Primary-source account of a major proof, worked out by humans directing AI agents. It is a counterpoint to the lab 'proof drops' and shows a workflow other researchers can copy.

items.title: AI designs functional enzyme components that could help expand drug discovery
items.excerpt: HIPS researchers combined pretrained AI models with experiments to design 76 new thiolation domains for non-ribosomal peptide synthetases. Several worked in living cells, and some raised product yields up to threefold over natural versions (Nature Communications, 10.1038/s41467-026-77963-6).
items.rationale: AI protein design checked in the wet lab: designed NRPS domains work in cells and raise yields up to 3x. This is biosynthesis biology with no specific disease, so it belongs in science, not medicine.

items.title: New neural framework could make LLMs more empathetic
items.excerpt: Georgia Tech researchers built a 'capability provenance' framework that traces which training-data sources drive an LLM's behaviour. Auditing Olmo 3, they found that stronger social reasoning and empathy came from interpersonal dialogue data such as FAQs and customer-service chats, not from textbooks (COLM; arXiv 2606.19625).
items.rationale: A fresh cognitive-science-of-AI finding: tracing a model's training data shows that empathy and social reasoning come from dialogue data, not textbooks (COLM paper on the open model Olmo 3).
